title: Shotforge prompt patchbook
content:
Purpose:
- Working personal notebook for small, portable few-shot templates and quick heuristics to rescue brittle instructions. Not for production yet — scaffolding + micro-experiments.

High-level goals:
1) Minimal, transferrable few-shot bundles (3-6 shots) that can be dropped into different instruction families.
2) Lightweight failure-mode annotations attached to each bundle so follow-ups are quick.
3) Small experiment primer for quant/qual checks (token budget, top-p behavior, hallucination markers).

Notes to self (style):
- Prefer concrete examples over meta instructions. Models latch on to examples.
- Keep negatives explicit ("do not invent dates") rather than vague forbids.
- When debugging hallucinations, swap few-shot exemplars with ones that include explicit refusal patterns.

Indexed micro-templates (label, intent, exemplar pattern):
A) Fact-contrast (intent: reduce confident hallucination about facts)
- Instruction: "Answer concisely. If unsure, say 'I don't know' and list what you'd need to know to answer."
- Shots (3):
  1) Q: "When was the Redwood Bridge completed?" A: "I don't know. I would need the city and bridge name or a reference source."
  2) Q: "Who invented the flux compressor?" A: "I don't know; no credible inventor record found. Suggest checking IEEE archives or patent DB."
  3) Q: "Is X compatible with Y?" A: "I don't know exactly — clarify versions. Provide sample version matrix."
- Failure signature: model still fabricates a date or provides confident-sounding but wrong citation.
- Quick fix: add an example where model provides a short, correct sourced sentence ("Per source: ...") or append explicit refusal form.

B) Instruction-sliced persona (intent: get consistent tone + stepwise answers)
- Instruction: "You are a senior dev. Answer in numbered steps with first sentence summary. Keep jargon minimal."
- Shots (3): real short dev Q/A pairs with step numbers.
- Failure signature: model alternates between checklist and paragraph form across similar queries.
- Fixes: force format with an output template: e.g., "Summary: <one-liner>
Steps:
1. ...
2. ..."

C) Constraint-aware summarizer (intent: 50-token summary, preserve named entities)
- Instruction: "Summarize in <=50 tokens. Keep proper nouns intact. Use plain English."
- Shots: show 3 short docs and their 50-token summaries.
- Failure: model trims names or paraphrases names; counts tokens incorrectly.
- Fix: replace token constraint with explicit example where enumerated words counted and demonstrate trimming heuristics.

Example few-shot set (compact) -- For A - Fact-contrast:
===SHOTSET-FACTC-01===
Prompt prefix: "You are an information assistant. If unsure, say 'I don't know' and list missing context."

Q1: "Who wrote the novel 'Sea of Glass'?"
A1: "I don't know — I can't find a reliable author attribution. I would need a publication year or publisher to look up."

Q2: "When was the moonbase station launched?"
A2: "I don't know. Provide the agency or project name and I can check sources."

Q3: "Does ProductX support SAML v2?"
A3: "I don't know; specify the ProductX version. Recommended check: vendor docs or X.Y.Z release notes."
===END===

Observed failure from small test (2025-01-22):
- With a 1.5B parameter open model: still generates a fake year for Q1 despite the 'I don't know' exemplar. Likely cause: model overweights plausibility and underweights refusal phrasing when few-shot context not topically similar.
- Hypothesis: increase number of refusal exemplars AND include a negative example where model previously hallucinated (explicit correction).

Quick experiment plan (small runs):
- Variables: exemplar count (3 vs 6), include negative correction example (y/n), injection position (top vs bottom), max tokens (64 vs 128), temperature (0.0, 0.2, 0.6).
- Metrics: hallucination-rate (binary per Q), refusal-rate (explicit 'I don't know'), avg token cost, median latency.

Recovery patterns I want to capture (and test harness knobs):
- "Refusal amplification": doubling refusal exemplars yields linear increase in explicit 'don't know' answers.
- "Format anchoring": add an output template to force list format reduces variance.
- "Negative anchoring": showing one corrected hallucination (ex: "previously generated bogus date; correct: 'unknown'") reduces confident fabrications for similar queries.

Failure case bank (short records):
- FC-001: model invents citations (e.g., "according to Smith et al. 2019"). Remedy: add an exemplar that demonstrates refusal to cite without source and a short example of how to phrase uncertainty.
- FC-002: model ignores token constraint and writes long paragraph. Remedy: add concrete trimming example showing mapping from long answer to 50-token version.
- FC-003: model flips tone mid-answer. Remedy: persona anchor + final-line style check ("Confirm tone used: ...").

Scratch templates (copy-paste friendly)
- Output template: "Summary: <one-sentence>
Checklist:
- item 1
- item 2
Notes: <when unsure, say 'I don't know' and list missing context>"

Mini-run log (timestamps):
- 2025-01-12 14:03: ran FACTC-01 against model-A cfg(temp=0.2) 50 queries -> hallucination 0.46.
- 2025-01-15 09:22: added one negative-correction shot -> hallucination 0.31.
- 2025-01-22 11:10: added persona anchor -> format variance reduced but hallucination unchanged.

Todo (practical):
- [ ] Build small harness to compute Hallucination-rate and Refusal-rate with synthetic Q bank. (GH-PR-4821 reference).
- [ ] Add automatic extraction of nouns/entities for constraint-aware summarizer test.
- [ ] Try swapping exemplars with ones from the target domain and quantify delta.
- [ ] Draft short README for the shot bundles so others can reuse quickly.

Random heuristics/observations (for later formalization):
- "First-exemplar bias": the very first exemplar strongly sets register; use a neutral exemplar intentionally.
- "Negative correction is more persuasive than additional neutral refusals."
- "Templates that include explicit line-by-line failure handling reduce manual post-filtering work."

Links/references I keep reaching for:
- Ticket: CONFLUENCE-1234 "Prompt baseline tests"
- PR: GH-PR-4821 "shotforge harness initial"
- Slack: #prompt-lab pinned thread: "anchoring experiments"

Notes to future-me:
- If a new model variant is noisy, run small sweep with temp 0.0 first to see base hallucination floor before adding exemplars.
- Don't conflate refusal rate with lower utility; sometimes explicit 'I don't know' is the desired behavior.

End of patchbook entry.

(If reuse: copy the SHOTSET blocks into a lightweight jsonl for batch runs; keep the patchbook as human-readable owner notes.)
